extracted.intended_audience: general public; government officials and civil society practitioners interested in Open Government Partnership membership and processes
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the standards, eligibility metrics, governance norms, and procedural requirements that govern Open Government Partnership (OGP) membership, action-plan co-creation, reporting, and oversight. Useful for governments and civil society preparing to join or to engage with OGP processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Government Declaration — acknowledge demand for openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should acknowledge that people worldwide are demanding more openness in government, including greater civic participation, and seek more transparent, responsive, accountable, and effective governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a normative principle signaling that participating countries should recognize citizen expectations for openness and responsiveness; it underpins commitments and is part of the Declaration that member governments agree to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Government Declaration — recognize national contexts and stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating countries recognize they are at different stages in promoting openness and will pursue approaches consistent with national priorities, circumstances, and citizens' aspirations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGP explicitly allows for variation in reform approaches and does not mandate a one-size-fits-all program—assessments and expectations are applied with respect for national context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Government Declaration — accept responsibility to strengthen commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries accept responsibility to seize the moment to strengthen commitments to transparency, fight corruption, empower citizens, and harness new technologies to make government more effective and accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This commits signatories to active reform and to using OGP as a vehicle for measurable improvements in governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Government Declaration — uphold openness in engagement with citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments must uphold the value of openness in engagement with citizens to improve services, manage public resources, promote innovation, and create safer communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle encourages governments to embed openness in public-facing practices and service delivery, not just in formal declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration commitment: increase availability of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants declare commitment to increase the availability of information about governmental activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the concrete expectations in the Declaration; ties directly to evaluation metrics such as access to information and fiscal transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration commitment: support civic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants commit to supporting civic participation in public affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen as a core component of open government and is evaluated (e.g., citizen engagement metric and co-creation expectations for action plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration commitment: implement highest standards of professional integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants commit to implementing high standards of professional integrity within government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normative commitment frames anti-corruption and ethical conduct as part of OGP aims; enforcement/assessment may link to IRM findings and membership expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration commitment: increase access to new technologies for openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants commit to increasing access to new technologies to promote openness and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages use of digital tools in transparency, service delivery, and citizen engagement; reflected in action-plan ambitions around technological innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility scoring system (overall requirement to join)
rubrics_metrics.description: To participate, governments must demonstrate commitment across four key areas measured by objective indicators and validated by independent experts; countries can earn up to 16 points (or 12 if one metric is not measured) and must earn 75% of applicable points (12/16 or 9/12) to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formal, quantitative gate for membership: independent validation of indicators determines eligibility; meeting the 75% threshold (of applicable points) is required before a simple ministerial letter completes joining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility metric — fiscal transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiscal transparency is one of the four critical areas used to evaluate a country's demonstrated commitment to open government for OGP eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by objective indicators and contributes to the points total used to determine whether a country meets the eligibility threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility metric — access to information
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to information is one of the four critical areas used to evaluate eligibility for OGP membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured with objective indicators and independently validated; directly connected to the Declaration’s commitment to increase availability of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility metric — asset disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Asset disclosure (public officials' asset disclosure regimes) is one of the four critical areas used to evaluate eligibility for OGP membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms part of the anti-corruption and integrity assessment that contributes points toward the eligibility threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility metric — citizen engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizen engagement is one of the four critical areas used to evaluate eligibility for OGP membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by objective indicators (e.g., legal/policy frameworks or practices enabling participation) and contributes to the overall points score for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement to join (ministerial letter and contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an eligible country to join, the required paperwork is a letter from a ministerial representative indicating agreement with the Open Government Declaration and intent to participate, plus designation of the leading agency and an individual point of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting the eligibility scoring threshold is necessary but the formal act of joining is completed by this ministerial-level notification and identification of responsible contacts for future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-creation of National Action Plans (NAPs) with civil society
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating countries must co-create National Action Plans with civil society; action plans are the principal instrument for developing agreed reforms/commitments on a two-year cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective public consultation during NAP development is encouraged to build broad support and relies on active collaboration between government and civil society; co-creation is central to OGP legitimacy and implementation monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action-plan expectations: content and cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Action plans should contain commitments aimed at advancing transparency, accountability, participation, and/or technological innovation; countries operate on a two-year action-plan cycle, continuously implementing and reporting on programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries are encouraged to pursue ambitious, novel commitments and to build on past successes; regular reporting and continuous implementation are required features of the cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Reporting Mechanism (IRM) — scope of assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRM produces biannual independent progress reports assessing governments on development and implementation of OGP action plans and their progress in upholding open government principles; reports also provide technical recommendations for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM assessments are intended to stimulate dialogue and promote accountability between governments and citizens; they evaluate both process (consultation/co-creation) and substance (implementation outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Experts Panel (IEP) — oversight of IRM quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Experts Panel oversees the IRM to help ensure quality of reviews, assess procedures, and promote findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IEP provides an additional, expert quality-control layer for the IRM to safeguard credibility of assessments used by stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of parity in governance bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP's steering committee and subcommittees preserve parity by including equal numbers of government and civil society representatives; leadership rotates with a new government co-chair and civil-society co-chair appointed annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parity is a structural rule intended to ensure multi‑stakeholder governance and shared decision-making across OGP bodies (Steering Committee, subcommittees).

rubrics_metrics.name: OGP Support Unit — neutral secretariat functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A small permanent secretariat (OGP Support Unit) maintains institutional memory, manages external communications, supports membership, and acts as a neutral third party between governments and civil society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Support Unit’s neutrality and continuity are presented as operational safeguards to help balance relationships and sustain OGP activities across membership cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding expectations — country contributions and donor complements
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP funding comes from country contributions (core, unrestricted funds), bilateral agencies, and private foundations; country contributions are expected and scaled based on World Bank income classifications with additional consideration for GDP size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Steering Committee sets minimum and recommended contribution levels (published tables of minima/recommended amounts per income/GDP bracket); bilateral/private funding may support specific initiatives but core functions rely on member contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and accountability mechanism for consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OGP process requires government consultation with civil society and citizens when drafting and implementing commitments, and the IRM specifically assesses the quality of this consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of stakeholder consultation is a formal dimension of IRM assessment, affecting perceived legitimacy and accountability of action plans and their implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-level participation standard (OGP Local)
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP Local extends OGP principles to sub-national governments; participating local jurisdictions develop action plans with civil society and are assessed by the IRM similar to national members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local participation was piloted and expanded; local jurisdictions are expected to follow co-creation, reporting, and IRM assessment norms analogous to national members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exit or suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries may leave or be removed from OGP for reasons including inactivity, formal government request to withdraw, or permanent suspension by the OGP Steering Committee (e.g., following Response Policy reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents historical examples (withdrawals, inactivity, suspensions); these are practical enforcement/exit mechanisms that reflect expectations for active participation and compliance with OGP policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Parliament engagement — parliamentary transparency commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP encourages parliamentary transparency, public participation, and accountability; however, parliamentary commitments are not always co-created in the same process as a country's OGP action plan and may rely on collaborations (e.g., OPeN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This highlights that legislative-institutional reform may follow different co-creation pathways and partnerships; OGP supports but does not strictly standardize parliamentary processes within NAP co-creation.
